The core insight of CPT lies in its dual treatment of probability and value: it uses rank-dependent weights π_i derived from cumulative probabilities to reflect bounded rationality, while applying a value function v(·) that captures loss aversion and diminishing sensitivity. In the context of GSI, these weights are fitted to synthetic user preferences to infer latent reward structures. For GSE, the CPT value function computes expected utilities over stochastic robot actions, enabling risk-aware navigation. The failure mode arises when π_i approaches zero or v(·) loses monotonicity, leading to invalid policy updates. The framework assumes fixed reference points and linear reward mappings, which may not generalize to complex environments without empirical calibration.
